segments.he: אֲבָל לֹא מָכַר אֶת הָאֲבָנִים שֶׁאֵינָן לְצׇרְכָּהּ. לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר – דְּלָא מְתַקְּנָן, לְרַבָּנַן – דְּלָא מַחֲתָן.
segments.en: The Gemara proceeds to explain the second half of the mishna, which teaches: «But he has not sold» along with the field «the stones that are not» designated «for use» in the field. On the assumption that the mishna speaks of stones that are placed on the sheaves to prevent them from being scattered, «according to Rabbi Meir,» the mishna is referring to stones «that are not ready» to be used for this purpose, whereas «according to the Rabbis,» even if the stones are ready to be used to protect the sheaves, they are not included in the sale if «they are not» yet «placed» on them.
